rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea seeks pardon for negligence and carelessness that lead to forgetfulness or error, since such causes fall within human responsibility.
rows.anchor: بما صدر عنا من الأمور المؤدية إلى النسيان أو الخطأ من تفريط وقلة مبالاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request implies that accountability for forgetfulness and error is possible because avoiding them is possible in some measure; otherwise the prayer would be meaningless.
rows.anchor: فإن التحرز عنهما في الجملة ممكن ولولا جواز المؤاخذة في النسيان والخطأ لم يكن للسؤال معنى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says this community is exempted from liability for error, forgetfulness, and coercion; earlier communities were liable for the first two.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان وما استكرهوا عليه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣr denotes a heavy load that pins its bearer in place, and here means burdensome religious duties.
rows.anchor: والإصر العبء الثقيل الذي يأصر صاحبه أي : يحبسه مكانه

words: كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelites faced severe duties: self-killing in repentance, cutting mistaken limbs and impurity, fifty daily prayers, mosque-only prayer, fasting restrictions, forbidden good things, quarter-wealth alms, and written records of nightly sins.
rows.anchor: وهو ما كلفه بنو إسرائيل من قتل النفس في توبة وقطع الأعضاء الخاطئة وقطع موضع النجاسة

words: كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: God spared this community comparable strictures and earlier peoples' punishments; the Prophet describes his mission as the easy, tolerant upright way and says his community is spared sinking, metamorphosis, and drowning.
rows.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم "بعثت بالحنيفة السهلة السمحة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This asks deliverance from unbearable punishments, after asking to avoid the onerous duties whose neglect could bring them; punishment is described as a load because those duties lead to it.
rows.anchor: واستعفاء من العقوبات التي لا تطاق بعد الاستعفاء مما يؤدي إليها من التكاليف الشاقة

rows.speaker: التيسير
rows.claim: The request means not to impose duties that are difficult to sustain continually; it does not ask for the literally impossible, which cannot occur.
rows.anchor: قال في "التيسير" أي : لا تكلفنا ما يشق علينا الدوام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pardon means removing the traces of sins; forgiveness means concealing faults so the believer is not exposed before people.
rows.anchor: أي : آثار ذنوبنا {واغفر لنا} واستر عيوبنا ولا تفضحنا

rows.speaker: التيسير
rows.claim: The two requests are not repetitive: pardon leaves the person unpunished and erases the sin, while forgiveness hides it from view; one may pardon while still mentioning and exposing a deed.
rows.anchor: قال في "التيسير" وليس بتكرار. فإن الأول تركه حتى لا يؤاخذ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers ask both that God overlook their sins and conceal them, so their state is not publicly exposed.
rows.anchor: والمؤمنون أمروا أن يسألوا التجاوز عنها وإخفاءها حتى لا يظهر حالهم لأحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pardon and forgiveness precede the request for mercy because clearing away faults comes before adorning the servant with favor.
rows.anchor: لما أن التخلية سابقة على التحلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlānā can mean our master while we are His servants, our helper, or the one who manages our affairs.
rows.anchor: سيدنا ونحن عبيدك أو ناصرنا أو متولي أمورنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea asks God to help against disbelievers and repel their harm, as a guardian should defend those in his care; victory may come through conquest, argument, or defense.
rows.anchor: أي : أعنا عليهم وادفع عنا شرهم فإن من حق المولى أن ينصر عبيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for victory also seeks protection from devils, since they belong among the disbelieving enemies.
rows.anchor: والنصرة على الكفار تكون بالظفر وتكون بالحجة وتكون بالدفع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Miʿrāj report, at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary in the sixth heaven, the Prophet received the five prayers, the closing verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness for any follower who avoids associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: فأعطى رسول الله عليه السلام ثلاثا أعطى الصلوات الخمس وأعطى خواتيم سورة البقرة

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: During the Miʿrāj, the Prophet recited the believers' response to 2:285 and then asked the petitions of this verse; God answered that error, forgetfulness, and coercion were lifted and granted the remaining requests.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في خبر المعراج : "قربني الله وأدناني إلى سند العرش

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says two verses from Paradise's treasures were written by the Merciful's hand two thousand years before creation, and reciting them after the final evening prayer suffices for night vigil.
rows.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم "أنزل الله آيتين من كنوز الجنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara will be sufficed, either for night prayer or for the reckoning on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم "من قرأ آيتين من آخر سورة البقرة كفتاه"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Bursevi uses the Prophet's designation of al-Baqara as the Quran's tent to refute disapproval of calling it Surat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "السورة التي تذكر فيها البقرة فسطاط القرآن"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet urges learning al-Baqara as a blessing, says abandoning it brings regret and sorcerers cannot master it, and the report links a house without its recitation for three nights with Satan's approach.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "السحرة" أي : لا تستطيع البطلة أن تسحر قارئها

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muʿādh used to say amen whenever he completed Surat al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وكان معاذ إذا ختم سورة البقرة يقول آمين

rows.speaker: أبو الأسلم الديلمي
rows.claim: Al-Daylami reports Muʿādh's capture of a date-stealing jinn; the Prophet foretold its return, and on its second capture it claimed that reciting al-Baqara's ending keeps devils out of a house that night.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الأسلم الديلمي قلت لمعاذ بن جبل : أخبرني عن قصة الشيطان حين أخذته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal particle idh is governed by an understood imperative meaning remember.
rows.anchor: {إذ} منصوب باذكر {قالت امرأت عمران} وهي امرأة عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman is Hannah daughter of Faqudha, wife of ʿImran ibn Mathan, mother of the Virgin Mary, and grandmother of Jesus.
rows.anchor: وهي امرأة عمران بن ماثان أم مريم البتول جدة عيسى عليه السلام وهي حنة بنت فاقوذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi distinguishes this ʿImran from ʿImran ibn Yashhar, father of Miriam, Moses and Aaron's sister: Zachariah's guardianship shows Mary was ʿImran ibn Mathan's daughter, and Zachariah and ʿImran were contemporaries; Zachariah married Mary's sister, making John and Jesus cousins.
rows.anchor: كفى بكفالة زكريا دليلا على أنه عمران أبو البتول لأن زكريا بن أذن وعمران بن ماثان كانا في عصر واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hannah was barren into old age; seeing a bird feed its chick stirred her wish for a child, and she vowed to dedicate a child to serve the Temple; she conceived Mary and ʿImran died during the pregnancy.
rows.anchor: بينا هي في ظل شجرة بصرت بطائر يطعم فرخا له فتحركت نفسها للولد وتمنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her vow was an act of gratitude: if granted a child, she would give the child to the Jerusalem sanctuary as one of its attendants.
rows.anchor: قالت : اللهم إن لك علي نذرا شكرا إن رزقتني ولدا أن أتصدق به على بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vow is something a person makes binding upon himself.
rows.anchor: والنذر ما يوجبه الإنسان على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the nonhuman relative pronoun for the child because the child's status was unknown and the fetus was not yet at the level of rational persons.
rows.anchor: عبر عن الولد بما لإبهام أمره وقصوره عن درجة العقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarraran means freed for Temple service, beyond the mother's use or employment, or wholly devoted to worship without worldly work or marriage.
rows.anchor: أي : معتقا لخدمة بيت المقدس لا يد لي عليه ولا أستخدمه ولا أشغله بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such dedication was lawful for them: children otherwise owed service to their parents when capable, and a vow released them for sanctuary service; prophets had dedicated offspring, and only boys were normally dedicated because menstruation and impurity required girls to leave.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا النذر مشروعا عندهم لأن الأمر في دينهم أن الولد إذا صار بحيث يمكن استخدامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hannah dedicated the fetus without qualification either because she assumed it would be male or because she used the vow as a means of asking for a son.
rows.anchor: ولكن حررت حنة ما في بطنها مطلقا إما لأنها بنت الأمر على تقدير الذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accepting means taking something with approval; Hannah asks God to accept what she vowed.
rows.anchor: أي : ما نذرته والتقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her request for acceptance is really a request for a son, since acceptance presupposes an existing offering and, by their custom, a girl could not be accepted for Temple service.
rows.anchor: وهذا في الحقيقة استدعاء للولد إذ لا يتصور القبول بدون تحقق المقبول بل للولد الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the infant proved female, Hannah's emphatic statement that she had delivered a girl expressed regret at her frustrated hope; the attached pronoun refers to the infant, and female is its circumstantial predicate.
rows.anchor: التأكيد للرد على اعتقادها الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God magnifies what Hannah delivered: she did not know Mary's extraordinary rank and that she and her child would become a sign for the worlds, so she grieved without knowing the gift's true worth.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى إنها لا تعلم قدر هذا الموهوب والله هو العالم بالشيء الذي وضعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The desired male would at best have been an ordinary Temple attendant, whereas the gifted girl surpassed him through the great events God would bring about through her.
rows.anchor: ليس الذكر الذي كانت تطلبه وتتخيل فيه كمالا قصاراه أن يكون كواحد من السدنة كالأنثى

words: وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلْأُنثَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both clauses are divine parenthetical remarks between Hannah's statement that she delivered a girl and her statement that she named her Mary.
rows.anchor: اعتراضان بين قول أم مريم {إنى وضعتهآ أنثى} وقولها : {وإنى سميتها مريم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary means worshipper or servant of the Lord in their language; Hannah names her to seek closeness and protection while reaffirming the vow despite having a girl.
rows.anchor: فإن مريم في لغتهم بمعنى العابدة وخادم الرب وإظهار أنها غير راجعة في نيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In her request for refuge, her offspring is coordinated with the object pronoun referring to Mary.
rows.anchor: عطف على الضمير المنصوب أي : أولادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording suggests ʿImran had died before Mary's birth, since convention assigned naming a newborn to the father rather than the mother.
rows.anchor: وظاهر هذا الكلام يدل على أن عمران كان قد مات قبل وضع حنة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root meaning of rajm is throwing stones; the epithet also means expelled.
rows.anchor: وأصل الرجم الرمي بالحجارة وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says Satan touches every newborn except Mary and her son; God protected them through the blessing of Hannah's invocation.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "ما من مولود يولد إلا والشيطان يمسه حين يولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Mary in place of the boy in Hannah's vow and became her guardian, bringing her to her proper maturity.
rows.anchor: أخذ مريم ورضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر {ربها} مالكها ومبلغها إلى كمالها اللائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The acceptance was gracious because the customary law permitted dedication only of a capable, rational boy, yet God received Hannah's baby girl in response to her plea.
rows.anchor: وهو قبول تلك الأنثى مع أنوثتها وصغرها فإن المعتاد في تلك الشريعة أن لا يجوز التحرير إلا في حق غلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her good growth is a metaphor for excellent upbringing that suited every circumstance of her life.
rows.anchor: مجاز عن التربية الحسنة العائدة عليها مما يصلح في جميع أحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recounts the acceptance because of Hannah's weakness, sincerity of intention at the beginning, and modesty at the end.
rows.anchor: وذلك لضعفها وصدق نيتها في الابتداء وحيائها في الانتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although four thousand people were dedicated to the sanctuary in that era, Mary's story alone became widely known.
rows.anchor: وكان في ذلك الزمان أربعة آلاف محرر لم يشتهر خبر أحد منهم اشتهار خبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant should see personal shortcoming even after striving, so God may accept the work through visible insolvency and hidden sincerity.
rows.anchor: وفيه تنبيه للعبد على أن يرى من نفسه التقصير بعد جهدها ليقبل الله عملها لإظهار إفلاسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God removes both seekers and those who have arrived from seeing their own works and states, though for different reasons: seekers lack verified sincerity, while the arrived are eclipsed by witnessing God as the true actor and themselves as instruments.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه سبحانه قطع السائرين له وهم المريدون والواصلين إليه وهم المرادون عن رؤية أعمالهم

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: When Abu ʿUthman al-Maghribi's disciples said their shaykh taught obedience and awareness of its shortcomings, al-Wasiti called this pure Magianism and urged witnessing the One who originates and directs the act instead.
rows.anchor: ولما دخل الواسطي نيسابور سأل أصحاب الشيخ أبي عثمان المغربي بم يأمركم

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri clarifies that al-Wasiti meant to protect disciples from self-admiration, not to settle them in deficiency or permit neglect of proper conduct.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري وإنما أراد الواسطي صيانتهم عن محل الإعجاب لا تعريجا في أوطان التقصير

rows.speaker: النهرجوري
rows.claim: A sign that God has taken charge of one's deeds is seeing deficient sincerity, heedlessness in remembrance, imperfect truthfulness, slack striving, and poor attention to poverty; one then finds every state unsatisfactory, grows needful of God, and fades from all besides Him.
rows.anchor: قال النهرجوري من علامة من تولاه الله في أعماله أن يشهد التقصير في إخلاصه والغفلة في أذكاره

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو العباس
rows.claim: Explaining 22:61, Abu al-ʿAbbas says obedience can be tainted by vanity, reliance, contempt for others, and demand for reward, while sin can be surrounded by humility, recourse to God, and esteem for the sinless; seekers should strive without being deceived by worship.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو العباس رضي الله عنه في إشارة قوله تعالى : {يولج اليل فى النهار ويولج النهار فى اليل}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alchemy poem likens spiritual effort to burying and spending gold in pursuit of a process that turns copper into pure gold; seekers should expend resources for divine approval and arrival at God's presence, even wealth and life, until the door of spiritual opening is reached.
rows.anchor: ه زرها بخاك سيه دركنند كه باشد كه روزى مسى زركنند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verse says gold is a good means to buy things, but reaching the Friend's presence is a better purchase, underscoring the goal of spiritual striving.
rows.anchor: زر ازبهر يزى خريدن نكوست ه خواهي خريدن به ازوصل دوست

rows.speaker: الشيخ الشاذلي
rows.claim: Al-Shadhili teaches that each kind of obedience contains lights of the unseen realm; missing a kind means missing its corresponding light, and spiritual inspirations do not replace regular litanies or acts of worship.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ الشاذلي قدس سره في "لطائف المنن" : واعلموا أن الله أودع أنوار الملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintain every form of obedience, then forget one's deeds to avoid vanity: preserving an act is harder than performing it, as brittle glass breaks irreparably and good deeds can be erased by wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: فينبغي للعبد أن يواظب على أصناف الطاعات وينساها بعدما عملها كيلا يبطلها العجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means God entrusted Mary to Zachariah, made him her guarantor, and charged him with her welfare; a kafīl provides for someone and tends their interests.
rows.anchor: بمعنى وضمنها الله إلى زكريا وجعله كافلا لها وضامنا لمصالحها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith compares the Prophet and the guardian of an orphan to two adjacent fingers.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين" وهو زكريا بن أذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah is identified as son of Adhan ibn Muslim ibn Sadoon and a descendant of Solomon son of David.
rows.anchor: وهو زكريا بن أذن بن مسلم بن صدون من أولاد سليمان عليه السلام ابن داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hannah wrapped Mary, brought her to the Temple, and presented her to Aaron's descendants, its custodians like the Kaaba's keepers; they competed for the daughter of Israel's leading family, while Zachariah claimed her because her maternal aunt was his wife.
rows.anchor: روي أن حنة حين ولدت مريم لفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد ووضعتها عند الأحبار أبناء هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Twenty-seven priests drew lots at the Jordan by casting pens they used to write revelation; after three rounds Zachariah's pen rose above the water while the others sank, so he received Mary's guardianship.
rows.anchor: فألقوا فيه أقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها الوحي على أن كل من ارتفع قلمه فهو الراجح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miḥrāb may be a chamber built for Mary that she reached by ladder, the most honored/front part of an assembly, or simply the name for their mosques.
rows.anchor: قيل : بنى لها محرابا في المسجد أي : غرفة تصعد إليها بسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only Zachariah entered Mary's chamber, and after he left it was shut behind seven doors.
rows.anchor: روي أنها لا يدخل عليها إلا هو وحده فإذا خرج غلق عليها سبعة أبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah found unusual food sent from Paradise: summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer; Mary had never suckled at a breast.
rows.anchor: إذ كان ينزل ذلك من الجنة وكان يجد عندها في الصيف فاكهة الشتاء وفي الشتاء فاكهة الصيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wondered where food unlike ordinary worldly provisions came from, out of season and despite her locked doors, with no one able to bring it in.
rows.anchor: من أين يجيء لك هذا الذي لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا وهو آت في غير حينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary was very young and unable to comprehend the question or formulate an answer; reports say she spoke in childhood, as Jesus spoke in the cradle.
rows.anchor: مريم وهي صغيرة لا قدرة لها على فهم السؤال ورد الجواب قيل تكلمت وهي صغيرة

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision without reckoning means abundant provision, provision without accounting, or provision from an unexpected source; this explains how Mary's food came from God.
rows.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو بلا محاسبة أو من حيث لا يحتسب وهو تعليل لكونه من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers to the stories of Hannah, Mary, Jesus, Zachariah, and John.
rows.anchor: ما ذكرنا في القصص من حديث حنة ومريم وعيسى وزكريا ويحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unseen news is available only by witnessing it, reading a book, learning from a scholar, or revelation; the first three means were absent for Muhammad, so revelation is the explanation.
rows.anchor: التي لا يوقف عليها إلا بمشاهدة أو قراءة كتاب أو تعلم من عالم أو بوحي من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation of these stories proves Muhammad's prophethood and establishes an argument against those disputing him.
rows.anchor: دلالة على صحة نبوتك وإلزاما على من يحاجونك من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic waḥy can mean revelation to prophets, inspiration, conveying a desired meaning, or a signal; all senses share the idea of informing in concealment.
rows.anchor: والوحي في القرآن لمعان للإرسال إلى الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's absence from the disputants over Mary's care confirms revelation; deniers know he neither read books nor learned these stories from scholars, and eyewitnessing was impossible.
rows.anchor: عند الذين اختلفوا وتنازعوا في تربية مريم وهو تقرير لكونه وحيا

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says deniers have only the absurd alternative of claiming eyewitnessing; they abandon the proven explanation of miracles for an impossible one, exposing their foolishness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في حواشيه : كأنه قيل : أيها المنكرون لأن أوحي إليه والمتهمون في دعوى نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The priests cast their pens used to write the Torah as a blessed way to draw lots over who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة اختاروها للقرعة تبركا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is linked to an omitted verb indicated by cast: they cast the pens to see or learn which person would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف دل عليه يلقون أقلامهم أي : يلقونها ينظرون أو ليعلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause refers to their dispute over Mary's care, already recounted above.
rows.anchor: في شأنها تنافسا في كفالتها وقد ذكر فيما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away after the covenant, its confirmation, acknowledgment, and testimony makes the deniers transgressors who leave obedience; a fāsiq in any group exceeds its bounds.
rows.anchor: الميثاق والتوكيد والإقرار والشهادة

rows.speaker: التيسير
rows.claim: Al-Taysir says prophets cannot turn away or be called sinful: either the covenant bound prophets and, dependently, their communities, so only the communities turned away, or prophetic immunity does not remove the trial.
rows.anchor: قال في "التيسير" والتولي لا يقع من الأنبياء ولا يوصفون بالفسق لكن له وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the covenant was in their scriptures and they knew Muhammad's prophethood was true, only enmity and envy explain their disbelief; like Iblis, they seek a religion other than God's.
rows.anchor: فقد كانوا عالمين بصدق محمد عليه السلام في النبوة فلم يبق لكفرهم سبب إلا مجرد العداوة والحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question coordinates with an understood clause: do they turn away and then seek a religion other than God's?
rows.anchor: عطف على مقدر أي أيتولون فيبغون غير دين الله ويطلبونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aslama means to submit sincerely and yield; those in heaven and earth means their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أخلص وانقاد {من فى السماوات والارض} أي أهلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who submit willingly are monotheists; deniers submit unwillingly through creation's signs, bodily changes, illness and health, wealth and poverty, joy and grief, and other states under God's decree.
rows.anchor: وهم الموحدون {وكرها} أي بإباء وهم الجاحدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All inhabitants return to God, warning rejecters of the true religion that none besides Him can bring harm or benefit.
rows.anchor: أي من فيهما والمراد أن من خالفه في العاجل فسيكون مرجعه إليه من حيث لا يملك الضر والنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person should obey God rather than break the covenant made on the primordial day.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يطيع ربه ولا يعصيه بنقض ما عهد إليه يوم الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant with prophets, saints, and believers is to affirm God's oneness, uphold religion without division, confirm one another, call people to obedience, and reserve worship for God; He asks sincere servitude and fulfillment of the Lord's rights.
rows.anchor: فعهد الله مع الأنبياء والأولياء والمؤمنين التوحيد وإقامة الدين وعدم التفرق فيه وتصديق بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: الشيخ الشاذلي
rows.claim: Al-Shadhili says it is an evident blessing when God grants obedience and then effaces the servant's awareness of it, relieving the outward self from disobeying Him.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ الشاذلي قدس سره : متى رزقك الله الطاعة والفناء به عنها فقد أسبغ عليك نعمة ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among God's mercies is explaining the paths of earlier people of guidance so later people can follow them and reach their aim.
rows.anchor: ومن جملة رحمته بيان طرائق من سلف وتقدم من أهل الرشاد ليسلكوا مناهجهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Gabriel explains that generous forgiveness means God pardons sins through mercy and then replaces them with good deeds through generosity.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : "يا كريم العفو" فقال جبريل أتدري ما معنى كريم العفو

rows.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
rows.claim: Rumi's Persian poem says God accepts repentance and transforms former sins into acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: قال جلال الدين الرومي قدس سره : توبه آرند وخدا توبه بذير أمر أو كيرند أو نعم الأمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is extra to emphasize the future sense inherent in wanting; the object of clarify is omitted and can be the hidden benefits and superior deeds or the lawful and unlawful duties.
rows.anchor: اللام مزيدة لتأكيد معنى الاستقبال اللازم للإرادة ومفعول يبين محذوف أي يريد الله أن يبين لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides believers to the paths of earlier prophets and righteous people so they may follow their example.
rows.anchor: أي يدلكم على مناهج من تقدمكم من الأنبياء والصالحين لتقتدوا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turns the addressed group from disobedience to obedience by enabling repentance from their former disagreement; the address is to a particular group who repented, not every accountable person, so the divine will is not unrealized.
rows.anchor: يرجع بكم عن معصيته إلى طاعته بالتوفيق للتوبة ما كنتم عليه من الخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the people addressed and is wise in what He wills for them.
rows.anchor: بكم {حكيم} فيما يريده لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause explains the full benefit of God's will and is not repetitive: the earlier clause described His willing to guide them to repentance, while this describes His accepting repentance toward them.
rows.anchor: بيان لكمال منفعة ما اراده الله تعالى وكمال مضرة ما يريد الفجرة بخلاف الأول فإنه بيان ارادته تعالى لتوبته عليهم فلا تكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those following desires are licentious people who obey their appetites; a person taking only pleasures allowed by religious law follows the law, not desire.
rows.anchor: يعني الفجرة فإن اتباع الشهوات الائتمار لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The licentious want believers to abandon truth by joining them in sexual misconduct and treating forbidden acts as lawful; this is a great deviation compared with an occasional sin without deeming it lawful.
rows.anchor: عن القصد والحق بموافقتهم على اتباع الشهوات واستحلال المحرمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lightens the burdens of duty by prescribing a tolerant, easy religious law and granting concessions in difficult circumstances, including marriage to bondwomen.
rows.anchor: ما في عهدتكم من مشاق التكاليف فلذلك شرع لكم الشرعة الحنيفية السمحة السهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are weak because they cannot reliably resist their appetites and powers, endure desires, or wield their strength through difficult acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: عاجزا عن مخالفة هواه غير قادر على مقابلة دواعيه وقواه
